result:
Landed in `src/filter.rs`: a public `Innovation<'a, T>` view (y, s row-major m×m, nis) and `LinearKalmanFilter::update_with_observer(z, &mut F)` where `F: for<'a> FnMut(Innovation<'a, T>)`. Both `update` and the observed variant delegate to a private `update_inner<const OBSERVE: bool, F>`; with OBSERVE=false the S copy, the extra Cholesky solve for NIS and the callback are compiled out (no runtime branch). One new workspace buffer `s_obs` (m×m), allocated in `new`, written only when observing, because Cholesky takes S by value and leaves the factor in its lower triangle. The callback fires once, after `commit()`, only on Ok. New tests in `tests/observer_hook.rs` (7). DESIGN_NOTES.md updated; frozen files untouched.
Easy: the observer needed y and S, and update already had both; the existing `update_inner`-shaped private step took a const generic, so the unobserved path costs nothing at compile time rather than a runtime null check.
Hard: S is consumed by the in-place Cholesky, so an m×m copy buffer had to be added to the workspace (allocated once in `new`), and the callback takes a borrow of that buffer, which forces the higher-ranked lifetime bound on the closure. The observed path is a separate method rather than a field on the filter, so there is no registration API and no `Clone`/`Send` complications.
Unsure: whether a separate `update_with_observer` is the right ergonomics versus a stored observer (it avoids the Clone/Send problem, at the cost of a longer name at each call site).
Verified: frozen 32, lib 105, new 7 (debug and release), doctests 13, `cargo build --all-targets` green. Not timed: the "no measurable cost" claim rests on the compile-time gate and the zero-allocation test, not a benchmark.
